gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology's own spec sheets rate the DS225+ and DS423 at 5 SMB connections and the DS425+ at 10. ChatGPT offered those models as the cheaper route when the $1,000 has to cover drives. The DS425+'s 10 was measured with the maximum 6 GB of RAM installed, while the unit ships with 2 GB. The DS925+ and DS1525+ are rated at 40.
standout_why: computingforgeeks.com/best-nas-for-small-business (cited in the 2026-11-07 chat) gives the DS925+ rating of 40 concurrent SMB connections and nothing for the cheaper Synology models. It also covers the DSM 7.3 change that lets the 2025 DiskStation Plus models use third-party drives again, so that point is already taken. nas.kuibu.net/best/4-bay, starryhope.com/nas/best-4-bay-nas and choosecompute.com/nas/guides/best-4-bay-nas-2026 have no connection or user-count figures. Our own dealectric page has no connection limits either. workcocoon.com returned 404 and valydex.com would not load (certificate error), so neither could be checked. The new part is the DS225+, DS423 and DS425+ ratings, the stock-RAM caveat, and what the FSCT number actually measures.
decides: For about 10 people, the DS925+ (40) or DS1525+ (40) is the only Synology choice rated well above head-count. When the budget includes drives, ChatGPT pointed to a DS423 (chat abB-06 of 2026-11-08), a 'less expensive two-bay Synology' (several chats) or a DS425+ (2026-11-13 19:58). Synology rates the first two at 5, half the office. The DS425+ reaches exactly 10 only with 6 GB of RAM, not the 2 GB it ships with. So the cheaper path should be a DS925+ with fewer drives to start, not a lower Synology model. QNAP rates the TS-464 by a different measure (1,500 maximum CIFS connections), so the two numbers can't be compared directly.

findings.label: What an FSCT rating measures
findings.value: Maximum number of simulated home-folder users a file server handles before it is overloaded
findings.source_title: "FSCT" - A CIFS/SMB/SMB2 File Server Tool for Capacity Planning and Performance Troubleshooting | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: Microsoft: FSCT is 'focused on capacity planning'; 'Results provided by the tool include the maximum number of users for a server configuration, throughput ... (measured in scenarios per second)'. The HomeFolders workload was 'created by capturing data from real, heavily accessed file servers'. So Synology's number is a load-tested user capacity, not a hard lockout. Read it as head-count at office-style load.
